scenarios.title: Find the checkout incident window
scenarios.brief: Support reports a brief checkout problem around a known time. Establish whether the report aligns with observable activity.

scenarios.title: HTTP error regression
scenarios.brief: HTTP 5xx responses increased after a release. Find the affected endpoint and a representative error.

scenarios.title: Authentication rejection surge
scenarios.brief: Sign-in failures have risen, but normal rejection types are mixed into the data. Isolate the abnormal reason and scope.

scenarios.title: Deployment version regression
scenarios.brief: Only part of the fleet appears unhealthy after a rolling deployment. Determine whether version is the differentiator.

scenarios.title: Rare error signature
scenarios.brief: A high-volume service contains one rare exception associated with failed requests. Isolate it and a correlated request.

scenarios.title: Schema drift and data quality
scenarios.brief: A dashboard count dropped even though traffic did not. Prove which producer stopped populating the expected field.

scenarios.title: Reduce log-pattern noise
scenarios.brief: A service emits thousands of repetitive warnings. Find the pattern that actually correlates with failures.

scenarios.title: Rank failing routes with ES|QL
scenarios.brief: Rank endpoints by failed request count and failure rate during the incident.

scenarios.title: Compare before and after deployment
scenarios.brief: Quantify whether a release materially changed latency and errors.

scenarios.title: Cross-service incident summary
scenarios.brief: Produce a concise result table showing volume, failures, and high-percentile latency across services.

scenarios.title: Dashboard incident triage
scenarios.brief: Use the supplied service overview to rapidly identify the affected region, service, and interval.

scenarios.title: Drill down from a dashboard spike
scenarios.brief: Confirm a chart spike at document level while preserving its filter and time context.

scenarios.title: Inspect dashboard panel calculations
scenarios.brief: Two supplied panels seem contradictory. Determine how each metric is calculated and which one answers the question.

scenarios.title: Slow dependency trace
scenarios.brief: Checkout latency is high. Find the downstream dependency and operation responsible.

scenarios.title: Trace error propagation
scenarios.brief: The edge service reports a generic failure. Find where the exception originated and how it propagated.

scenarios.title: Retry amplification
scenarios.brief: Latency and dependency traffic increased without a matching rise in user traffic. Prove whether retries amplified calls.

scenarios.title: Trace-to-log correlation
scenarios.brief: A failing trace lacks error context. Find the exact application log for the request.

scenarios.title: CPU saturation
scenarios.brief: One service slows during a traffic peak. Determine whether compute saturation aligns with the event.

scenarios.title: Memory leak and restarts
scenarios.brief: A workload becomes unstable over several hours. Find the resource trend and first restart evidence.

scenarios.title: Hot instance imbalance
scenarios.brief: Aggregate service health hides an outlier instance. Identify it and show that its peers remain healthy.

scenarios.title: Capacity and throughput saturation
scenarios.brief: Latency rises only above a traffic threshold. Estimate the saturation point from supplied evidence.

scenarios.title: Active alert triage
scenarios.brief: An alert fired for an unfamiliar service. Decide whether it represents an active customer issue and cite source evidence.

scenarios.title: Legacy slow checkout investigation
scenarios.brief: Users report that checkout became slow. Identify the bottleneck and support the conclusion with correlated request evidence.
